messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: Pager — Sev2: Canary pool 'canary-a' in us-west-2 showing elevated errors (5xx) and KMS decryption failures. Alert group: deploys.

oncall-bot: Incident channel created: #eng-oncall. Thread_ts=1779001234

devon: acked. I'm on it — pulling canary logs now. Anyone on releases? @jen

sara: I can help with KMS/keys — snooping logs.

jen: hmm saw the canary rollout started ~4m ago for the config/key-rotation change. Rolling out to 10% canary.

carlos: quick note: we rotated the customer-kms alias as part of the key-rotation job earlier, per rollout plan. It should be backward-compatible but maybe alias propagation lag?

devon: logs show repeated: `AccessDeniedException: User: arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/redwood-canary-role is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt on resource arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/0a1b2c3d4e`

devon: here's a snippet from the canary pod log:

```
2026-03-15T02:21:02Z ERROR decrypt_secret: kms.Decrypt failed: AccessDeniedException: Not authorized to perform kms:Decrypt on key 0a1b2c3d4e
    at com.redwood.secrets.KMSClient.decrypt(KMSClient.java:84)
    ...
```

jen: that smells like either the key ARN changed (new key id) or IAM policy didn't include new key id in the resource list. Did the rotation create a new CMK id?

carlos: rotation created a new CMK (id above). We aliased customer-key -> new-key-id as part of the canary. IAM role statements reference the alias ARN rather than literal key ids, so alias should cover it, but if alias hadn't propagated to the canary's region, deny is possible.

sara: i'm running `aws kms list-aliases --key-id 0a1b2c3d4e --region us-west-2` to confirm. Also checking key policy: `get-key-policy`

infra-bot: deploybot: canary rollout stage=1/10, traffic_shift=10% -> monitoring.

devon: customer impact? Any production traffic hitting canary? Product routing said canary had small % of non-critical internal customers and synthetic tests. Early indicators: 0.3% of API requests in us-west-2 saw 500s in the last 3m, mostly from internal test keys. No major customer-facing error spikes yet.

jen: still, we should stop the rollout and switch the flag to kill new config. Can someone flip the feature flag? I don't want more canaries to pick up the new key.

carlos: flipping flag now. Command: `curl -X POST https://flags.redwood/api/flip -d '{"flag":"key-rotation-2026-03","state":"off"}'` -> 200 OK

devon: confirmed: flag off. New pods won't pick up rotated key.

oncall-bot: Action taken: feature flag 'key-rotation-2026-03' toggled to off by carlos at 02:25Z.

sara: i can backfill a temporary role permission to let canary decrypt with the new key while we investigate. But that would broaden blast radius. Alternative: patch canary env to point to the previous key id (old-key-id 9z8y7x6w).

jen: prefer reverting canary config to old-key-id and then re-run rotation more carefully. Carlos, can you patch the canary's env var and trigger a restart?

carlos: patching deployment: `kubectl set env deploy/canary-a KMS_KEY_ID=9z8y7x6w -n prod-canaries` -> rolling restart initiated.

devon: restart done. Monitoring logs...

devon: canary logs now show successful decrypts and no 5xx for the past 30s. Health probes green.

oncall-bot: Update: canary-a health restored at 02:31Z. Error rate back to baseline.

sara: I'm going to run a quick permissions audit: checking key policy for the rotated key (0a1b2c3d4e) and the alias mapping. Looks like rotation created the key but the key policy didn't include the canary role's ARN — bug in rotation script where we only propagated alias but didn't attach key policy entries for consumer roles.

devon: that explains AccessDenied. Good catch.

jen: milestone: rollback of canary config complete, flag off, canary healthy. Let's assess customer impact and incident severity.

devon: severity: low->moderate. Limited blast radius, small percentage of internal/synthetic traffic saw 500s. No external customer tickets yet. Recommend Sev2 until root cause confirmed.

carlos: action items: 1) patch rotation script to update key policy and verify role ARNs (owner=infra) 2) add canary pre-check to verify key policy before alias switch 3) postmortem doc (owner=jen) 4) coordinate re-rollout with a stricter canary gate.

sara: i'm adding a temp automated check to the rotation pipeline to `aws kms get-key-policy` and `aws kms list-aliases` and fail the pipeline if consumer role not in policy. Will push a hotfix branch.

infra-bot: ci/build: rotation-pipeline-hotfix started by sara (PR #4921).

devon: handoff: i'm oncall for another 20m then handing to morning shift. I'll summarize for the handoff channel.

jen: thanks devon/sara/carlos. I'll create the incident ticket and start the postmortem draft with timeline and impact. Assigning to jen (owner) with infra and SRE as contributors.

devon: short post to #status-updates: "Brief service disruption for small subset in us-west-2 due to key rotation bug. Canary rollout halted and reverted. No sustained customer impact observed. Full postmortem incoming." :thumbsup:

oncall-bot: On-call handoff note: devon -> morning-oncall at 02:45Z. All implicated alerts silenced; monitoring watch continuing.

carlos: before we close thread: is there work needed to roll back the alias to old key permanently? We left alias pointing to new key, but canary env was reverted to old-key-id. We should coordinate alias/alias rollback and not leave a dangling config.

sara: good catch. I propose: 1) rotation-pipeline-hotfix merged and validated 2) revert alias to old key temporarily or update key policy to include canary role for new key 3) re-run rotation against a green canary. I'll make the change list in the PR.

jen: agreed. I'll include that in the runbook updates.

devon: closing the Slack thread for now. Will reopen if we see new errors. Thanks team.

oncall-bot: Thread closed by devon at 02:49Z. Incident state: mitigated.
